subject: Next steps & trial brief: model roster, language fallbacks for Cordova Labs
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@cordovalabs.com>, Priya Desai <priya@cordovalabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-08T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps & trial brief: model roster, language fallbacks for Cordova Labs

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed trial plan so we’re aligned before we kick off: 

Summary of needs (from discovery):
- Customer-facing product classification + taxonomy mapping across English + Spanish (primary), with occasional French throughput.
- Tight latency goals for interactive UX (p95 target), and strict cost sensitivity for scale.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 evidence and optional VPC/private deployment down the line.

Proposed trial objectives / success criteria:
1) Accuracy: taxonomy mapping F1 >= 0.90 on agreed eval set (we’ll co-author the eval prompts).
2) Latency: p95 generator latency < 350ms for 128-token responses in US region.
3) Cost: baseline per-token cost target we’ll set during the first week (benchmarking phase).
4) Stability: <2% error rate (timeouts/500s) during peak test window.

Model roster (recommended for the 4-week trial):
- Primary (fast, cost-aware): Mistral-7B-Instruct (8-bit quantized) — expected best latency/cost tradeoff for short completions.
- Fallback (robust instruction-following): Llama-2-13B-chat (quantized variant) — use when higher-context or safety sensitivity required.
- Long-form / highest-quality: Falcon-40B-Instruct (small sample set, not default) — subject to capacity.

Multilingual plan:
- Default prompt templates for EN/ES; character-level normalization and domain-specific tokens to be included.
- If Spanish drops below threshold, we’ll route Spanish requests to the fallback model until we tune prompts/LoRA or a lightweight finetune.

POC timeline (suggested):
- Week 0 (3 business days): kickoff, share trial scope workbook and eval prompts (attached).
- Week 1: ingest sample corpus, run baseline benchmarks (latency/cost), author eval set.
- Weeks 2–4: iterative tuning, prompt engineering, automated evals, acceptance run.

Owners / roles:
- Customer success / PM: Monica Patel (monica.patel@redwood.ai) — trial coordination, acceptance criteria sign-off.
- Engineering lead: Ben Carter (ben.carter@redwood.ai) — perf tests and model rollout.
- Sales / escalation: Jordan Blake (jordan.blake@redwood.ai) — commercial & milestones.

Attachments: trial-scope.xlsx (workbook), SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf (requested), perf-test-instructions.md (bench harness).

Please confirm this plan and the proposed success criteria — also flag anything we missed (on-prem needs, additional languages, procurement timelines). Once you confirm, we’ll book a 45-minute kickoff and Ben will schedule the perf run.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake | Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0198
From: Samir Shah <samir@cordovalabs.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya@cordovalabs.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps & trial brief: model roster, language fallbacks for Cordova Labs

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick notes from our side: 

- SOC2: the security/compliance ask is real — our infosec needs the SOC2 evidence and high-level architecture diagram before we allow any sample data onto hosted endpoints. Priya is looped for procurement.
- On-prem: we don’t need full on-prem yet, but we do require the option to run the inference runtime in our VPC (private deployment) if the trial surfaces PII. Can you include the VPC quickstart in the kickoff?
- Success criteria: we agree with accuracy and latency but can we make latency a bit looser for the first benchmark window (p95 < 450ms) and then tighten after tuning? We prefer a ramp rather than hard cut.

Also, a clarification on models: we trust the Mistral recommendation for speed, but our product team prefers to see Llama-2-13B comparisons for Spanish handling. Can you ensure both are included in the baseline tests?

Available for a kickoff next Tue (2026-09-15) 10–11am PT or Wed 9–10am PT. Let us know which works.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Shah
Head of Product, Cordova Labs
samir@cordovalabs.com

Jordan — noted. I’ll own the perf runs and baseline comparisons. High-level internal checklist for the trial: 

- Spin up two configs: (A) Mistral-7B-Instruct quantized w/ KV caching enabled; (B) Llama-2-13B-chat quantized without KV cache (to measure tradeoffs).
- Use the perf-test-instructions.md attachment for consistent harness (Aditya will template the scripts).
- Create prompt templates for EN/ES and run 1k synthetic queries + 200 customer-provided test items (Monica will collect PII-safe samples).
- Capture: p50/p95 latency, tokens per second, compute GPU utilization, and top failure modes.

I’ll post raw results in the Drive folder by EOD Friday (2026-09-10). If Samir wants the VPC quickstart, I’ll include steps for temporary peered subnet access during the trial.

—Ben
